sections.text_helper: Section 34.3.9 "Forced output mode" in chapter 34 (General-purpose timers (TIM12)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 1296.
sections.section_content:
In output mode (CCxS bits = 00 in the TIM_CCMRx register), each output compare signal
(tim_ocxref and then tim_ocx) can be forced to active or inactive level directly by software,
independently of any comparison between the output compare register and the counter.
To force an output compare signal (tim_ocxref/tim_ocx) to its active level, one just needs to
write 0101 in the OCxM bits in the corresponding TIM_CCMRx register. Thus tim_ocxref is
forced high (tim_ocxref is always active high) and tim_ocx get opposite value to CCxP
polarity bit.
For example: CCxP = 0 (tim_ocx active high) => tim_ocx is forced to high level.
The tim_ocxref signal can be forced low by writing the OCxM bits to 0100 in the
TIM_CCMRx register.
Anyway, the comparison between the TIM_CCRx shadow register and the counter is still
performed and allows the flag to be set. Interrupt requests can be sent accordingly. This is
described in the output compare mode section below.
